text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: tenant-isolation-alert for customer Vela (dedicated pool dp-88) — latency spike + inter-tenant KV prefix overlap detected. Pager: Alicia M. oncall.
Alicia M.: picking this up. reading alert: routing anomalies show a small fraction of requests (0.28%) hitting tenant prefix of another customer in dp-88. Are we seeing any PII or payloads cross-tenant?
Mateo R.: current prod KV logs show a mix of prefixes for ~11:42–11:49 UTC. I pulled a quick sample — truncated payloads only. No obvious PII in the sample, but need full evidence collection before claiming no exposure.
Priya S.: tagging Sarah (sec) and Raj (runtime). Raj — any recent kernel or routing changes to dp-88? We had a rollout for batching/eviction heuristics earlier today.
Raj P.: rolled config 11:30 UTC: kvcache-prefix-evict: aggressive=true on dp-88 as a rollback for hotspotting. The change was supposed to be safe but it touched routing logic for latebind ephemeral prefixes. Rolling back now if needed.
Dan O.: visibility: only dp-88 (us-west-2 dedicated) shows the pattern, not other pools. Might be latebind resolver returning stale prefix map. Could be a rare race: eviction + latebind mapping leads to prefix lease assigned to wrong tenant window.
Alicia M.: first action plan: 1) Stop writes to kvcache for dp-88 (maintenance mode) 2) Snapshot logs + sample payloads (redact PII) 3) Evict suspicious KV mappings with audit trail 4) Notify Vela primary contact (ops@vela) with initial status — non-blocking? do we have SLO impact?
Sarah K. (Sec): prioritize evidence collection. If we see any customer data outside tenant boundary, escalate to legal. For now assume potential exposure until proven otherwise. Need hashes of payloads and full request IDs for 11:40–11:50 window.
Mateo R.: running command to collect entries: ```bash
# pull kvcache access logs for dp-88 window
redwoodctl logs fetch --pool dp-88 --from 2026-03-15T11:40:00Z --to 2026-03-15T11:50:00Z --filter "kv_access OR routing_decision" > /tmp/dp88_kv_1140.json
jq '.[] | {ts:.ts, req_id:.req_id, tenant:.tenant, prefix:.prefix, sample:.payload|truncate(200)}' /tmp/dp88_kv_1140.json | gzip > /tmp/dp88_kv_1140.snip.json.gz
```
Mateo R.: dumps starting, ETA ~2m.
Priya S.: putting dp-88 into maintenance mode (write-protect) for minimal blast radius. Mateo, can we keep read path on? Vela is high-throughput; complete outage will be bad.
Dan O.: we can keep read-only. Exec: ```bash
redwoodctl pool update dp-88 --kv-mode read-only --note "isolation scrub in progress"
```
Dan O.: executed, status OK.
Raj P.: rolling back kvcache-prefix-evict change to the prior commit to rule out the config as cause. Deploy starts now.```bash
git checkout deploys/dp-88@2026-03-15-1100
deployctl start --pool dp-88 --component kvcache
```
Alicia M.: Mateo — once your log bundle is ready, run the evidence pipeline: redact, hash, store in evidence-bucket with ACL restricted to sec+oncall+eng-leads.
Mateo R.: bundle done. Pushed to s3://evidence-redwood/incidents/3300012345/dp88_kv_1140.snip.json.gz. Hash sha256: 3f7a9b... (will DM full).
Sarah K. (Sec): pulled. doing quick scan for identifiable patterns; initial scan shows 4 request payloads containing 'email' keys but those appear obfuscated (tokens). We'll do full regex/hashing.
Alicia M.: summarize customer impact: Vela reports elevated error rate 11:43–11:53 for certain endpoints. We suspect up to 0.3% of their requests might have hit neighboring tenant prefix mapping. So far no confirmed full payload exfiltration, but partial key overlap observed.
Priya S.: action item list so far: evidence collected (Mateo), pool in read-only (Dan), rollback started (Raj), sec scanning (Sarah), draft customer note (Alicia). Who will own customer comms?
Alicia M.: I can draft initial note. Proposed short message: "Hi Vela — we detected a small routing anomaly affecting dp-88 between 11:42–11:50 UTC. We've isolated the pool to read-only, are collecting logs, and currently have no confirmed data exposure. We'll update within 2 hours with findings." OK?
Priya S.: fine. Send after Sarah signs off on no confirmed exposure in initial scan. Also create incident channel/inc-report to track postmortem.
Alicia M.: drafting and will post in #incidents with subject line in internal doc.
Raj P.: rollback complete and verified. kvcache evict policy is back to previous behavior. No further config changes in the queue.
Dan O.: temporary mitigation: we flushed latebind cache and applied stricter lease validation on prefix assignment: ```json
{ "latebind_lease_ttl_ms": 2000, "lease_validation": "strict" }
``` applied to dp-88 control plane. Monitoring for reoccurrence.
Mateo R.: rerun sample query looking for tenant mingling after rollback/flushing. Quick result: no new cross-tenant hits after 11:56 UTC in the sample window.
Sarah K. (Sec): sec verdict (tentative): no clear evidence of full payload being delivered to the wrong tenant. We have 17 events where routing_decision referenced neighbor-prefix, but payloads truncated and encrypted by app-layer for most. Need to pursue full retention logs (longer-term) if customer requests deep audit.
Alicia M.: drafting customer message now. Mateo — include the evidence bundle link but redact sensitive items. Sarah — sign off before sending.
Sarah K. (Sec): OK to send high-level with sentence: "We have no confirmed data exposure; we are continuing a full audit and will share findings within 4 hours."
Alicia M.: sent to Vela ops@vela with cc to account manager. Copy pasted: "Hi — quick update: we've isolated dp-88 to read-only, collected logs for 11:40–11:50 UTC, rolled back a recent kvcache eviction change, and applied an additional validation patch. At this time we have no confirmed customer data exposure. We will follow up with a full audit within 4 hours and can provide signed evidence artifacts on request."
Vela SRE (via email): replied to Alicia privately saying they see reduced errors, appreciate the quick action; asked for ETA on full log sharing.
Priya S.: next steps: 1) preserve full retention logs (Mateo) 2) create a postmortem deck outline (Alicia + Dan) 3) schedule deep audit with sec + eng + legal if evidence shows anything further 4) consider mitigations platform-wide for latebind lease races.
Mateo R.: preserved full retention: redwoodctl retention copy --pool dp-88 --from 2026-03-15T11:30:00Z --to 2026-03-15T12:30:00Z --dest s3://evidence-redwood/incidents/3300012345/full_retention.json.gz. Tokenized and ACL'd.
Dan O.: moving to handoff: Alicia — you'll keep as lead for customer comms and postmortem. I'm on follow-through for remediation and RBAC tests. Alicia, can you take this to next oncall at 12:30Z?
Alicia M.: yes. I'll hand off to oncall-rotation at 12:30Z with a tidy summary and actions.
oncall-rotation: acknowledged. Please add a short runbook note: "if cross-tenant prefix detected, set pool to read-only, preserve retention, rollback recent kvcache/latebind changes, flush latebind cache, collect evidence bundle and notify sec."
Alicia M.: added runbook note.
Sarah K. (Sec): closing note: escalate to legal if customer requests full clearances or if any unredacted payloads are discovered. Keep a tight ACL on evidence. I'll start the deeper regex/hunt overnight and post findings.
Mateo R.: monitoring graphs show dp-88 error rates back to baseline and no new anomalies for 12 minutes. Closing pager for now, will reopen if new signals appear.
Alicia M.: wrapping up: thanks all. I'll post a short incident thread summary and create an internal postmortem ticket with severity P2. End of thread for now. :thumbsup:
